knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Owner or manager pressure is not release. The worker holds the job and documents the reason until the controlling authority's written release and an approved plan exist.
A general access code does not release a room under investigation. The room stays excluded and the authorised lead is told.
Privacy and dignity duties mean no photographs or details go to neighbours. The designated manager decides any disclosure.
A possible sharp is not opened, pressed or reached into. The response is isolate, withdraw and escalate to trained staff.
PPE is chosen from a documented hazard assessment and checked against the worker's training. Ordinary gloves and a disposable mask are not sufficient for an unidentified scene.
Unknown contamination is treated as a hazard until assessed. Appearance does not show the hazard is absent.
Zoning drawings are planning aids. They do not prove clearance, and suspected spread requires a new assessment.
A clean appearance does not establish decontamination. Porous and electronic items need a specialist decision and evidence first.
Waste is classified before packaging, transport or disposal, and only authorised carriers move regulated waste.
Equipment with an unknown exposure history is quarantined. Quick reuse can carry contamination to the next client.
A possible puncture is an exposure. Work stops, the protocol starts and clinical assessment follows. Pressure to finish the shift does not change this.
Limited specialist work does not support a building-wide safety claim. The handover withholds it and escalates the unresolved hazards.

practicalCriteria: Classifies a simulated post-incident request and lists each authority still to be confirmed, using a role-and-authority matrix and a hold notice.
Marks a fictional floor plan with excluded zones, stop points and a reassessment trigger, without any entry into a real scene.
Selects the correct stop, refer or continue decision for each simulated scenario and cites the trigger used.
Completes a scope-limited completion report that separates work done, checks, exclusions, unresolved hazards and referrals.
Explains in writing why the learner cannot make a forensic, biological-safety or habitability claim.
passRule: Competent only if all five observable tasks are demonstrated correctly in supervised, inert simulation with no critical safety failure. Critical failures include proceeding where a boundary is unmet, handling evidence or regulated material beyond the remit, or claiming clearance without authority. A written quiz pass is not practical competence. Not approved for use until subject-matter, legal and jurisdiction review is complete.
evidenceRequired: Role-and-authority matrix and hold notice for each simulated case.
Annotated fictional floor plan with excluded zones and escalation route.
Written stop, refer or continue decision with the trigger cited.
Scope-limited completion report from the simulated job file.
Assessor observation record signed by an organisation-authorised competent assessor.
stopWorkCriteria: Any entry or work where the police, coronial or other official release is unclear or absent.
Any disturbance, movement or photograph of potentially relevant objects.
Any disclosure of personal details or images to neighbours, family or media.
Any PPE selection that has not been approved against the hazard assessment and the worker's training.
Any unauthorised waste bagging, transport or relabelling.
Any reuse of equipment with an unknown exposure history.
Any unsupported clearance, forensic or habitability claim.
